claims.title: Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Unreliable Information Sources
claims.verification: Proceedings metadata, abstract and full PDF received
claims.transferable: Keep a primary-only baseline; reject unreliable auxiliary sources; account for final primary-source verification.
requirements: Target and sources drawn from known multi-output GP
Compact convex continuous domain, sufficiently smooth covariance and acquisition
Bounded GP derivatives with specified tail control
Registered pseudo-baseline construction and actual final primary observation
claims.important_limit: Theorem1 compares robust budget Lambda+lambda_primary to single-fidelity Lambda. It is not a same-budget distribution-free no-harm guarantee for finite-menu MAESTRO. Kernel/noise misspecification invalidates automatic transfer.

claims.title: Multi-fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Multiple Information Sources of Input-dependent Fidelity
claims.verification: Proceedings metadata, abstract and full PDF received
claims.transferable: Learn source/condition-dependent noise with uncertainty; compare against constant-noise and primary-only policies.
requirements: Correct target GP with specified kernel
Additive Gaussian source noise; independent observation-noise premise
Compact convex domain and derivative tail assumptions
Source noise bounded between registered minimum and maximum; learned noise marginalized
claims.important_limit: Heteroscedastic variance need not absorb systematic source bias or shared DMSO error. A GP theorem is not evidence that current A/B are exchangeable or informative about terminal B.

claims.title: muscat detects subpopulation-specific state transitions from multi-sample multi-condition single-cell transcriptomics data
claims.verification: Publisher full HTML and metadata received
claims.transferable: Use experimental samples as inference units; aggregate appropriate cell-level responses or use explicit multi-sample models.
claims.important_limit: Cells and cell halves within a source sample are not independent experimental replicates. A pseudobulk method does not authenticate cultures, exposure times or RNA utility.

claims.title: Systema: a framework for evaluating genetic perturbation response prediction beyond systematic variation
claims.verification: Publisher full HTML and metadata received
claims.transferable: Distinguish perturbation-specific variation from average/systematic shifts; use strong mean and matching baselines.
claims.important_limit: Primary experiments concern genetic perturbations. Published metrics/benchmarks do not establish MAESTRO chemical ranking correction, phenotype gains or source-repeat independence.
